name: Fresh Grated Ginger
tcm_energetic_impact: Warms the middle burner (Spleen/Stomach), dispels interior cold, and descends rebellious Stomach Qi to stop nausea.
western_nutritional_impact: Gingerol and shogaol compounds support gastric motility, may ease nausea, and offer mild anti-inflammatory action.
max_safe_dosage: Up to 1 tsp (approx. 2g) freshly grated per serving; do not exceed 4g/day.

name: Jasmine Rice
tcm_energetic_impact: Neutral in temperature; tonifies Spleen Qi, generates fluids, and is easy for a weakened digestive system to transform.
western_nutritional_impact: Low-fiber, highly digestible starch that provides steady glucose without taxing the GI tract.
max_safe_dosage: 1/2 cup dry rice per serving as a base staple; no restrictive upper limit for typical use.

name: Cinnamon
tcm_energetic_impact: Warms Yang, invigorates the movement of stagnant Qi and Blood, and dispels interior cold.
western_nutritional_impact: Cinnamaldehyde may support a healthy post-meal blood sugar response and has mild antimicrobial properties.
max_safe_dosage: Up to 1/2 tsp (approx. 1-2g) per serving; do not exceed 6g/day of cassia cinnamon long-term due to coumarin content.

name: Oats
tcm_energetic_impact: Neutral and gently tonifying to Spleen and Stomach Qi; moistens dryness without generating dampness.
western_nutritional_impact: Beta-glucan soluble fiber slows gastric emptying, can buffer stomach acid, and supports lasting satiety.
max_safe_dosage: 1/2 cup dry rolled oats per serving.

name: Peppermint
tcm_energetic_impact: Cool and aromatic; disperses Wind-Heat and moves stagnant Liver Qi to relieve distension.
western_nutritional_impact: Menthol relaxes GI smooth muscle, which may ease bloating and nausea (avoid if reflux-prone).
max_safe_dosage: 1 tsp dried leaf (or 1 small fresh sprig) steeped as tea, once per serving.

name: Toasted Sesame Oil
tcm_energetic_impact: Warm and nourishing; moistens Blood and lubricates intestinal dryness.
western_nutritional_impact: Monounsaturated fats add satiety and flavor without significantly increasing meal heaviness.
max_safe_dosage: 1 tsp per serving, added as a finishing oil (not for high-heat cooking).

name: Turmeric
tcm_energetic_impact: Warm and acrid; invigorates the movement of Qi and Blood to resolve stagnation.
western_nutritional_impact: Curcumin exhibits anti-inflammatory properties that may support general digestive comfort.
max_safe_dosage: 1/4 tsp ground turmeric per serving; up to 1 tsp/day taken with food.

name: Honey
tcm_energetic_impact: Neutral to slightly warm; tonifies Spleen Qi, moistens dryness, and harmonizes other ingredients.
western_nutritional_impact: Provides quick, simple-sugar energy and has a mild demulcent (soothing) effect on the throat and stomach lining.
max_safe_dosage: 1 tbsp per serving. Not suitable for infants under 12 months.

name: Sea Salt
tcm_energetic_impact: Neutral and descending; guides other flavors inward and softens hardness.
western_nutritional_impact: Trace sodium supports basic electrolyte balance at the small quantities used here.

name: Cardamom
tcm_energetic_impact: Warms the middle, moves Qi, and transforms dampness that contributes to a sense of fullness.
western_nutritional_impact: Volatile oils act as a carminative, traditionally used to reduce gas and support digestive comfort.
max_safe_dosage: 2-3 lightly crushed pods (or 1/4 tsp ground) per serving.

name: Fennel Seed
tcm_energetic_impact: Warm and moving; disperses cold stagnation lodged in the Stomach to relieve pain and distension.
western_nutritional_impact: Anethole compounds are carminative and traditionally used to ease bloating and gas.
max_safe_dosage: 1 tsp whole seeds, lightly crushed, per serving.

name: Chamomile
tcm_energetic_impact: Cooling and calming; settles the Shen (spirit) and soothes constrained Liver Qi.
western_nutritional_impact: Apigenin has mild calming properties and is traditionally used to ease GI spasm and support relaxation.
max_safe_dosage: 1 tbsp dried flowers steeped 5 minutes, one cup per serving.
